messages:
samir: Hey team — ISO fieldwork asking for an "access trace" package for inference-service covering the last 90 days. They want provenance from auth -> action -> storage. Quick sanity check: what concrete artifacts + exports should we hand over?

ana: high level: auth events (token create/renew/revoke), service-account role changes, admin console logins, deploy events, KMS decrypt events if applicable, and object-level S3 access logs for artifacts. Also include mapping doc that ties these logs to our control IDs.

jamie: Agreed. For each artifact include: 1) raw log sample (redacted) 2) a parsed CSV or JSON index with timestamps + user/service + action + request_id 3) query used to produce it 4) a short narrative linking it to the control objective.

samir: Cool. Any preferred query examples? auditor asked for an auditable trail showing a specific change (service principal update) and the path to workload impact.

jamie: For Splunk use something like:
```
index=redwood-prod source="auth" service="inference-service" request_id=ABC123 | table _time user action ip request_id context
```
For CloudWatch Insights (if some logs live there):
```
fields @timestamp, @message | filter requestContext.requestId = "ABC123" | sort @timestamp asc
```
Include the raw event and the parsed result CSV.

ana: For KMS ops, include key usage logs from CloudTrail: 
`eventName=Decrypt OR eventName=GenerateDataKey` with the requestId mapping. Redact ciphertext blobs but keep keyId, principal, and time.

mark_iso: From the auditor side — we need chain-of-custody justification. The CSV index + the queries are important. Also: demonstrate sampling methodology if you can't export full 90-day raw logs (size/PII). Provide sampling seed and deterministic selection method.

samir: Good point — we will not be able to hand over full raw logs due to size/PII. Proposed sampling: stratified by week + incident/request_id frequency, include 1000 records per week (or all records if week < 1000). Use a deterministic hash on request_id to pick samples. Is that acceptable?

mark_iso: That is acceptable if you document the exact algorithm (hash function, modulus, seed) and show reproducibility. Auditor explicitly called out determinism.

ana: Also, document retention policy: what we retain, for how long, and where. For ISO: they often expect 12 months+ evidence of retention enforcement. We keep auth logs 18 months in cold S3, audit indices 13 months in Splunk hot/cold. Add a small note about legal holds (if any).

jamie: Add a small sanitized replay demonstrating timeline reconstruction for a sample request: 1) auth token issued, 2) role binding change, 3) deploy job, 4) subsequent API call — stitch entries using request_id and git commit id. That really helps auditors see traceability.

samir: On redaction: what fields to redact? We should remove full user emails for external contractors, full IPs maybe last-octet masked? Any standard?

ana: Mask PII: emails -> user id mapping (provide mapping doc separately). IPs -> x.x.x.0 for IPv4. Do NOT redact request_id or keyId or principal arn. Those are needed for stitch.

mark_iso: Confirmed: keep identifiers that prove linkage, mask PII and payloads. Provide a redaction script and run output so we can verify.

sec-ops-bot: Automated export checklist: 1) run `scripts/export/audit_package.sh inference-service 90d` 2) collect `splunk_queries/` files 3) upload to presigned S3 path with MFA + audit log entry. See https://redwood.internal/docs/compliance/export-checklist

samir: I'll run export tomorrow morning. Jamie — can you add example queries and the deterministic sampling code to the compliance repo? Ana — can you draft the control mapping doc that ties each artifact to control IDs and narrative?

jamie: Yep, will push a PR with queries + `tools/sample_logs.py` that uses sha256(request_id) % 1000 < threshold. I'll include a README showing the seed and example run.

ana: On it — will draft mapping and the retention summary. I'll also include the legal-hold exceptions list.

samir: Thanks. Mark_iso — anything else we should include up front to avoid back-and-forth?

mark_iso: If you can include an execution checklist and an index file (top-level CSV) listing every artifact with path, query used to generate it, redaction status, and control mapping, that will reduce follow-ups. Also include timestamps when exports were created and who ran them (MFA user).

samir: Perfect. We'll follow that. I'll post the presigned link in this thread once it's uploaded. :thumbsup:

mark_iso: Looking forward to it. Thanks everyone.
